title: Northstar Bank — Private VPC deployment proposal (arch Q&A, Terraform notes, upgrade plan)
content:
Summary:
This is a customer-specific draft proposal for Northstar Bank (NSB). It covers a two-region VPC/on-prem hybrid private deployment for their fraud-detection model serving, Terraform module recommendations, BOM/sizing assumptions, and a phased upgrade plan for migrating from the current managed API to a Private deployment. The doc collects architecture Q&A from the last 3 design sessions and captures open decisions required before a formal SOW.

Scope and goals:
- Provide an HA inference platform in NSB-controlled networks (primary DC + DR site) with automated failover for inference traffic and audit-grade logging for PCI/financial controls.
- Support steady-state 120 concurrent inference sessions at 512 tokens average/response, with peak bursts up to 600 concurrent sessions for short windows (5–10 minutes).
- Maintain 99.9% availability, p95 tail latency <= 220ms for short-context scoring calls, and offline batch/embeddings throughput for nightly risk re-scoring.
- Ensure KMS/HSM integration for model keys and strict egress rules (outbound to Redwood control plane only via dedicated NAT and pinned IPs).

Assumptions (customer-provided + our defaults):
- NSB will provide two VPCs (primary in us-east-1 and DR in us-east-2) peered and with transit connectivity to on-prem core network for audit/monitoring collectors.
- Dedicated GPU fleet: initial commit for 4x A10G-equivalent nodes in primary, 2x in DR for warm standby. Autoscaling allowed for burst windows via reserved capacity and pre-authorized burst subnet.
- Expected token rate (steady): 120 sessions * 512 tokens * 0.5 tokens/sec average = ~15k tokens/sec. Peak burst token rate ~75k tokens/sec for ~10 minutes.
- Data residency: all inference data must remain in the VPCs; no raw logs shipped to public cloud S3. Aggregated telemetry can be exported to customer-hosted Splunk.
- Compliance: PCI-DSS and SOC2 required. NSB will handle SOC2 artifact sharing; Redwood will provide attestation for our private control plane components and the deployment automation steps.

Sizing and BOM (initial recommended):
- GPUs: Primary: 4x H100L- or A100s depending on model (we recommend testing 80B float16 optimized model vs 13B quantized). DR: 2x matching instance type for compatibility.
- CPU nodes for control plane/mgmt: 3x m6i.large equivalents (HA control plane), colocated in primary and one in DR for failover signaling.
- KV cache + runtime: 3x local NVMe 4TB per inference node for model shards/cache; ephemeral / persistent storage on separate RAID-1 for logs (500GB).
- Network: 25 Gbps NICs recommended on inference nodes to support burst batching.
- HSM: Dedicated HSM cluster (CloudHSM/Thales equivalent) with KMS policies; NSB to provision and share connection info.
- Observability: Agent collectors (Fluent Bit) to send aggregated metrics to Splunk via TLS to NSB endpoints. No customer PII in logs.
- Terraform-controlled components: VPC, subnets, route tables, security groups, SG bastion, private ECR/registry, instance profiles, autoscaling groups, and RBAC bindings for the Redwood private control plane.

Network & HA design notes:
- Active/passive model routing: primary region handles traffic; DR remains warm with model sync via S3-compatible private replication at off-peak hours. Failover triggered by control-plane health checks and a DNS TTL of 60s managed via NSB's internal DNS service.
- Egress lock-down: only allow outbound to Redwood control plane IP list and NSB audit collectors. No direct internet access from inference pods.
- Service mesh: optional mTLS between control plane components and workloads; plan includes cert rotation scripts using the HSM-backed signing flow.

Terraform module notes (practical guidance):
- Module layout recommended: modules/vpc, modules/network-peering, modules/compute-instance, modules/gpu-asg, modules/hsm-connector, modules/registry, modules/monitoring. Keep modules small and idempotent.
- State: Use remote state in NSB-managed backend (Terraform Cloud or S3 with state-locking). Sensitive variables must be supplied via TFVARs at apply time through the SRE runbook; do not commit secrets.
- Version pins: pin provider versions; use module versioning with semver. Redwood will provide example module registry entries in the PR link above.
- Lifecycle hooks: add null_resource hooks for pre-bootstrap (install GPU drivers, container runtime) and post-bootstrap (model pull into local NVMe). Use remote-exec only with controlled bastion sessions.
- Idempotent upgrades: design modules so that rolling upgrades are possible by creating new ASG launch templates + controlled instance termination. Avoid in-place immutable changes to NVMe layout.

Upgrade/Migration plan (phased):
Phase 0 — Kickoff & discovery (2 weeks):
- Verify network reachability and HSM access. Export inventory of current API usage patterns (sample traces) from NSB.
- Run PoC perf tests with representative prompt sets.

Phase 1 — PoC (3 weeks):
- Deploy single-AZ minimal cluster (1 GPU node) in NSB VPC, run Canary traffic (5% of live). Validate TLS, HSM, logs.
- Validate TF modules and document required IAM roles/policies for NSB.

Phase 2 — Pilot (4 weeks):
- Expand to full primary capacity (4 nodes), integrate autoscaling policy and prefix caching. Route a small subset of production customers (10–15%) to private deployment.
- Monitor latency/cost, adjust batching configs.

Phase 3 — Cutover & DR test (2–3 weeks):
- Gradual shift to primary handling 100% of traffic with canary rollback windows. Run DR failover drill (DNS flip + control-plane failover) to validate RTO < 5 minutes.

Phase 4 — Harden & handover (2 weeks):
- Complete compliance checklists, run audit logging verification, formalize runbook with on-call escalation matrices, and handoff to NSB operations.

Rollback strategy:
- Use DNS with low TTL and traffic-weighted routing for quick rollback. Keep the prior managed endpoint available for up to 48 hours post-cutover for rapid failback.
- Maintain snapshot/AMI images of inference nodes pre-upgrade for rollbacks to previous runtime.

Operational runbook excerpts (quick wins):
- Healthchecks: control-plane heartbeat plus per-node NVMe health and GPU temperature checks. Automate alerting to NSB PagerDuty.
- Scaling: prefer vertical batching parameter adjustments for short bursts. Autoscaling should be conservative (scale-up based on token-queue depth, scale-down after 10m of low activity).
- Cost control: enable per-token metering on the private control plane and chargeback CSV exports to NSB billing team weekly.

Architecture Q&A (collected):
Q: Can models be pinned to different quantization profiles per tenant?
A: Yes — runtime supports serving the same model binary with different quantization profiles; the TF modules will deploy model-variant subfolders and an alias map.

Q: How will we handle model updates without downtime?
A: Rolling deploys via new launch-templates + staged traffic shift. For large model warm-up, use a three-step pre-warm: pull -> instantiate minimal VM -> warm KV cache -> join rotation.

Q: Is a private control plane required or can we use Redwood-hosted control plane?
A: Customer requires control-plane telemetry to remain inside NSB network for compliance. We will deploy the control plane components in NSB VPC (private control plane). Some telemetry may still flow to Redwood for SLA telemetry via the pinned IPs if agreed.

Open questions / decisions needed from NSB:
- Final confirmation on GPU family (H100 vs A100) given cost and model selection (80B vs 13B).
- HSM vendor selection + on-prem connectivity windows for secure key exchange.
- DNS management: does NSB want Redwood to manage DNS flip or will NSB ops control cutover?
- Required RPO for model replication between regions (near-real-time vs nightly).

Next steps / action items:
- Redwood to run a short perf matrix (3 model variants) on target GPU types and share numbers by 2024-11-20.
- NSB to provision HSM test instance and a VPC with two peered subnets by 2024-11-29.
- Schedule follow-up workshop to finalize Terraform module variable interface and roles (agenda: secrets handling, remote state, bastion process).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a rough draft intended to capture decisions from our last calls. Numbers are conservative; final sizing will be updated after the perf PoC. Please mark any compliance-related gaps and highlight if additional network constraints exist (e.g., air-gapped requirement).

Appendix (short checklist):
- [ ] PoC perf runs completed
- [ ] HSM connectivity verified
- [ ] TF modules merged into NSB fork with state backend configured
- [ ] DR failover drill scheduled
- [ ] Compliance artifacts collected

End of document.
